claims.text: At stage-2 POST /api/v1/orders answers 201 Created with a Location header pointing at the new order (CreatedAtAction to Get).

WebApplicationFactory<TEntryPoint> starts the app from its entry point (Program.cs) inside the test process on an in-memory TestServer; CreateClient() returns an HttpClient whose requests reach it without Kestrel or a network port.

ApiFactory derives from WebApplicationFactory<Program> and implements IAsyncLifetime; InitializeAsync starts its PostgresFixture (Database: start + MigrateAsync) and a RedisContainer redis:8.10.2-alpine.

ConfigureWebHost: UseSetting("ConnectionStrings:Default"/"ConnectionStrings:Redis", ...); Program.cs reads GetConnectionString("Default"/"Redis"); the lab passes ConnectionStrings__Default/__Redis as env vars. Redis's has no user; PostgreSQL's names the user.
At stage-2 Program.cs applies no migrations (comment lines 89-92: the migrate service runs the migration bundle first).

WebApplicationFactory builds the app (the host) lazily on first use such as the first CreateClient(); xUnit awaits ApiFactory.InitializeAsync before the class's first test, so the database is migrated before the app builds.
claims.source_hint: ApiFactory.cs:13-17 comment; aspnetcore-docs integration-tests; xunit shared-context; verified by execution (OrdersApiTests pass)

claims.text: ConfigureTestServices callbacks run after the app's own service registrations in Program.cs, so a registration added there replaces or adds to the app's.

ApiFactory's ConfigureTestServices removes IEmailSender registrations (RemoveAll), registers Emails (FakeEmailSender) as singleton, and adds TestAuthHandler as default scheme; nothing else is replaced.
In API tests NotificationSender (hosted service) still runs and sends through IEmailSender, which is FakeEmailSender recording each email.

PostOrder_SignedInCustomer_Returns201WithLocation inserts a customer and a product, posts via PlaceOrderAsync(ClientFor(...)), asserts 201 and Location /api/v1/orders/{id}; OrdersApiTests resets via factory.Database.ResetAsync().

Creating a controller with new and calling its method skips middleware and authorization (which decide whether it runs) and routing, which matches method and path to the endpoint and builds the URL for Location.

Replace only what needs an outside server (a mail server behind IEmailSender; sign-in, next lesson) and keep PostgreSQL and Redis real; then the order id in Location is one PostgreSQL assigned, as in the lab.

With Docker running, `dotnet test DonHang.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~OrdersApiTests"` passes 5 tests; docker events (image filters postgres:17.6-alpine, redis:8.10.2-alpine, event=create) shows one create for each image.
